## North star

> Revise **BA 815 (MBA Business Statistics, Smeal)** for 2026: keep the statistical backbone and course
> structure, but **integrate AI throughout**, replace written quizzes with **AI-run audio oral exams**, open
> the tool track beyond R to **Python and Excel**, add a **course project**, and **refresh the examples** — so
> students learn both statistical inference and how to work with AI as analysts.

The course teaches data types (categorical vs continuous — different data demands different math),
summarization, and **statistical inference**: whether a relationship found in a random sample holds in the
general population. Delivered through general linear models — regression, logistic regression, ANOVA, and
dummy-variable regression. **Structure is retained; this is a revamp, not a redesign.**

## Why next

The syllabus is John's first deliverable and it forces every other decision — assessment weights, tool
policy, AI use policy, oral-exam structure, and the project spec all have to be stated in it. Session 1's
orientation deck must then be consistent with it, so E2 cannot start first.

**One trap to respect:** the syllabus must state the assessment structure, but **E3 (AI oral exams) decides
whether that structure is feasible at all.** Publishing a syllabus that promises AI-run oral exams before the
spike proves they work — at this class size, within accommodation requirements, with defensible grading — is
the way this project goes wrong in front of students. So the E3 spike should run far enough to establish
feasibility *before* the syllabus locks, even though E3 finishes much later.

## Note on how this campaign was captured

John described this project to the steward several times and got the same dialog box back each time with
nothing written. Root cause is recorded in `COURSE-REVAMP-BRIEF.md` Appendix C: the scaffolding path is
zero-model by policy and matches a closed verb list that omits the words he actually used, so his full
